origin: Founded in 1830 in Plum Run, Pennsylvania, USA by John Rich.

craft_evidence.owned: Heritage claim only: brand site says John Rich built a woolen mill at Plum Run, PA in 1830. Evidence of closure: last US plant (Woolrich, PA) announced closed Sept 2018 (Wikipedia citing WSJ 21 Dec 2018; WSJ not read). No current owned facility evidenced; live range made in India, Turkey, Romania, I
craft_evidence.makers: NONE (0 of 13 men's PDPs name a maker; YKK zips and PrimaLoft padding named only as components)
craft_evidence.mills: NONE on the live men's range (0 of 13; "recycled Italian wool blend" unnamed). Manteco and Kuroki appear only in collection names with no live men's product on 2026-10-10.
craft_evidence.heritage: Dated and placed (brand claim): "1830: John Rich builds first woolen mill in Plum Run, Pennsylvania"; timeline with 1850 Buffalo Check shirt, 1861-65 Union Army blankets, 1925 Pennsylvania Tuxedo, 197
craft_evidence.process: NONE: PDPs give fabric descriptions and certifications (RDS down, Control Union CU 884067) only; no making process published.
craft_evidence.reasoning: Every one of the 13 live men's styles states a country of origin (India, Turkey, Romania, Indonesia, Vietnam, China), but none names a maker or mill and no process is documented. The 1830 Pennsylvania mill is heritage only: the last US plant at Woolrich, PA was announced closed in 2018. A dated, placed founding story over contract-made product reads as a 2.

ownership.owner: Split by territory. Outside Europe incl. US: Baoxiniao Holdings Co., Ltd. (China; listed Shenzhen) bought the Woolrich IP in June 2025. Europe: BasicNet S.p.A.

opview: “By studying those objects closely, we can understand what has endured and decide what is worth carrying forward.” — Woolrich, Woolrich Heritage page
